summary: M1b adds what MSI, Burn, COM and system objects need: an ownership index (MSI tables and component clients of every installed product, all users and contexts; SharedDLLs; Installer\Folders; Burn dependents), harvest for MSI and Burn installs (including an install folder derived from component key paths, the 7-Zip MSI case), 14 new scanners and one extended (COM-CLASS, COM-INTERFACE, COM-SHELLEX, SYS-SERVICE, SYS-TASK, SYS-FIREWALL, SYS-APPX extension, SYS-BURNDEPS, FS-PKGCACHE, FS-WER, REG-ARP-MSI, REG-SHAREDDLLS, REG-INSTFOLDERS, REG-PRIVACY, REG-DIAG), and execute plus undo for three new action kinds: delete service, delete scheduled task, delete firewall rule. MSI-registration cleanup and COM registrations need no new action kind: they are key and value deletes behind narrow guard exemptions. 38 packages in 8 waves. The design is written against the code at 3265797 (branch m2), not against ENGINE_PLAN where the two differ; every difference is listed in plan_corrections. Three rules shape everything: (1) no scanner reads the registry or the disk on its own, and M1b adds no whole-registry or whole-volume walk: the one post-uninstall reference walk is computed once and shared, and the ownership index is built once per run and shared; (2) an object or a value is offered only when all of it is the app's, and attribution is by program path or installer record, never by name; (3) a typed action is bound at act time to the identity digest recorded at scan time, has a verified definition backup, a typed inverse, declared fault points and a hive flush before any record that vouches for its effect.

text: enum Scope { Value, Key, Path, Package, Object }. Scope::of(Target::Service | Target::Task | Target::FirewallRule) = Some(Scope::Object). Scope::ALL has 5 entries. ScopeSet gains bit 0x10 for Object; ScopeSet::ANY includes it; every other existing named set is unchanged.
enum ManifestKind { Inno, Msi, Burn } (serde names "inno", "msi", "burn" following the existing rename rule of the enum).
New EvidenceKind::OwnedSystemObject: default tier A, weight 8, scope set {Object}. No other evidence kind changes tier, weight or scope.

New soft blockers: Blocker::ReversibilityPartial (the undo cannot restore everything, for example a service account password) and Blocker::ProgramUnresolved (the object's program path could not be resolved to one file). New hard blockers: Blocker::Driver, Blocker::HasDependents { names: Vec<String> }, Blocker::ObjectChangedSinceHarvest. Existing blockers keep their serde form.

Component key path data format (value data under ...\Installer\UserData\<sid>\Components\<packed component>\<packed product>): a file path "C:\dir\file.ext"; a file path with '?' as the second character ("C?\dir\file.ext") meaning the file is reference-counted in SharedDLLs (shared_dll = true; the '?' is replaced by ':'); a registry key path "NN:\Key\Name" where NN is 00 HKCR, 01 HKCU, 02 HKLM, 03 HKU and 20-23 the same roots in the 64-bit view; an empty string or a path ending in a backslash (directory key path). A value named 00000000000000000000000000000000 marks a permanent component and is kept in clients as such.

A path-keyed store is a key whose value NAMES are full file or directory paths. In such a store a value is the app's when its name, decoded as the store requires, is a full path inside an InstallRoot of the fingerprint or equal to one of its exe paths. A bare file name never matches. A match on value data never counts here.
enum PathStore { SharedDlls, InstallerFolders, AppCompatLayers, PcaStore, PcaPersisted, MuiCache, UserAssist, FeatureUsage }
SharedDlls: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\SharedDLLs and HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\SharedDLLs. Name = file path.
InstallerFolders: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Installer\Folders. Name = directory path, usually with a trailing backslash.
AppCompatLayers: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\AppCompatFlags\Layers and HKU\<sid>\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\AppCompatFlags\Layers. Name = file path.
PcaStore: HKU\<sid>\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\AppCompatFlags\Compatibility Assistant\Store. PcaPersisted: the sibling key Persisted. Name = file path.

MuiCache: HKU\<sid>\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\MuiCache (also reachable as HKU\<sid>_Classes\Local Settings\...). Name = file path followed by ".FriendlyAppName" or ".ApplicationCompany"; the suffix is stripped. Names starting with '@' (resource references) are never matched.

UserAssist: HKU\<sid>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\UserAssist\{GUID}\Count. Name = ROT13 of a path that may start with a known-folder GUID in braces; decode ROT13 (ASCII letters only), expand the known-folder GUID through the known_folders source data, then test. Names that decode to something that is not a path (UEME_ counters, AUMIDs) are never matched here.

FeatureUsage: HKU\<sid>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FeatureUsage\{AppBadgeUpdated, AppLaunch, AppSwitched, ShowJumpView}. Name = file path or AUMID; only the file-path form is matched here.
Every key above is added to purge_guard::containers::VALUE_CONTAINERS, so the key itself can never be offered and only single values can.

rules: Open with MsiOpenDatabaseW(path, MSIDBOPEN_READONLY). Never MsiOpenPackage*, MsiOpenProduct*, MsiInstall*, MsiConfigure*, MsiReinstall*, MsiProvide*, MsiUseFeature*, MsiGetComponentPath on behalf of repair. An xtask rule (M1B-SCAN-INTEG adds it) greps purge-win for those names.

A table that does not exist gives an empty list. Any other error on one table gives Err for the whole package (the caller then treats the package as unreadable; partial tables must never look complete).
Limits: TableLimits { max_rows: 200_000, max_cell: 65_536 }. Hitting max_rows sets truncated and stops reading that table. A cell longer than max_cell sets truncated.
Every MSIHANDLE is closed on every path (RAII guard). The file is opened without write access and with share-read; a file that is not an MSI gives Err, not a panic.

Value name = packed product code (client), data = key path in the format of C-OWNERSHIP. Uses RegistrySource::walker with at most `threads` workers (default 8), depth exactly 2 below Components; nothing else under UserData is read here.
A client is counted for every user and context: the same component under UserData\S-1-5-18 and under UserData\<user sid> gives the union of clients.

A client that is not an installed product in `products` (stale registration) is still a client. It is reported in clients_of as found; whether a stale client blocks is the caller's decision (it does: see M1B-HARVEST and scanners; only the target product itself is ever discounted).

Registry key paths (NN:) are mapped to canonical keys: 00/20 -> HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes for machine context and HKU\<sid>\Software\Classes for user context; 01/21 -> HKU\<sid> of the UserData sid (S-1-5-18 maps to the literal HKU\* 'any user'); 02 -> HKLM with the 32-bit view (WOW6432Node inserted by the existing guard mapping, which knows the shared and redirected keys); 22 -> HKLM 64-bit view; 03/23 -> HKU. The mapping is one call into purge-guard per key; this package contains no list of redirected keys.

MSI rows: for every installed product with an MsiInfo.local_package: tables from the cache or from sys.msi_tables; rows resolved by msi_rows.rs. Root -1 follows the product's context (Machine -> 2, user contexts -> 1). Formatted keys: [ProductCode], [UpgradeCode], [ProductName], [ProductVersion], [Manufacturer] and any property present in MsiTables.properties are substituted; '[[' and other Formatted syntax ([#file], [$component], [!file], [%ENV], {..} groups, [\x] escapes other than the four bracket escapes) make the row unresolved: it is dropped and counted. An unresolved row never produces a broader guess.
The 64-bit attribute of the row's component (Component.Attributes bit 256) selects the registry view; a component missing from the Component table makes the row unresolved.
whole_key is true only for Registry rows whose Name is '-' or '*' and whose Value is null.
A package that cannot be read (NotFound, AccessDenied, truncated, any error) puts its product in unreadable(); its rows are unknown. The index never treats 'unreadable' as 'owns nothing'.

SharedDLLs: values() of both SharedDLLs keys; name canonicalised as a file path, data must be REG_DWORD (other types -> count unknown = Some(u32::MAX), which blocks). Installer\Folders: value names canonicalised as directories.

Burn: for HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\Installer\Dependencies and every HKU\<sid>\Software\Classes\Installer\Dependencies: each provider key's Dependents subkey names. Provider key names are compared case-insensitively.

Cache: TableCache keyed by (local_package canonical path, size, mtime) taken from fs.metadata at build time. Cache files are one JSON per key (file name = SHA-256 of the key), read with a 16 MiB cap, schema string purge.msitables/1 checked, and any parse failure is a cache miss (never an error, never partial data). MemTableCache is provided for tests and for unelevated runs.

packages.title: purge-harvest: MSI facts, install folder from component key paths, Burn bundle facts, system objects recorded before uninstall

model.why: Decides the install root for MSI apps and which services, tasks and rules count as the app's; a root that is too wide makes every later scanner dangerous.

packages.scope: Fill Fingerprint.msi, .burn and .sys (C-FP) and derive install roots for MSI installs that register no InstallLocation and no DisplayIcon (7-Zip MSI). New steps in the fixed harvest order: after 'machine facts': build OwnershipIndex and SysObjectIndex; after 'identity': msi facts and burn facts; inside 'roots': MSI component roots; after 'anchors': anchors from the app's own MSI tables (Class, ProgId, TypeLib, AppId rows add to fp.anchors); after 'refsnap': system objects.

consumes: existing validate_root, RootSource::MsiComponent, AppFileOutsideRoot handling in roots.rs

rules: pub fn harvest_report_with(entry, inventory, sources, baseline, kb, opts: &HarvestOpts) where HarvestOpts { pub table_cache: Option<&dyn TableCache> }; harvest_report keeps its signature and calls it with no cache.

MSI facts: for the target entry when InstallerKind is Msi, and for every MSI child of a Burn bundle (below). components = ownership.components_of(packed) with other_clients = clients_of(component) minus this product's packed code. registry_rows, services from the product's own tables through the same row resolver as the index (purge_index::ownership::msi_rows; no second resolver). package_readable false leaves rows empty and adds the warning 'msi package unreadable'.

MSI root rule (R-MSI): take the file key paths of components whose other_clients is empty. Drop every path under %SystemRoot%, under a Package Cache root, under Common Files\microsoft shared, and every path for which validate_root rejects all ancestors. Group the remaining paths by their highest ancestor directory that validate_root accepts (the 'top'). A group yields a root only if it has at least 2 key-path files, or it has 1 and its directory equals the directory of the MSI Property ARPINSTALLLOCATION/INSTALLDIR-style value found in fp identity or of a shortcut target already harvested. The root is the lowest common ancestor directory of the group's files; it must itself pass validate_root and ownership.dir_components(root) must list no component with a client other than this product (stale clients count as others). The root gets RootSource::MsiComponent.

Key-path files that fall in no root become AppFileOutsideRoot entries (for example C:\Windows\py.exe would, if it were not under %SystemRoot%: files under %SystemRoot% are recorded in fp.outside_root_files only when the component has no other client, and they are never roots).
A component with any other client contributes nothing: no root, no outside-root file, no anchor.
If the ARP entry gives an InstallLocation, the M1a root logic is unchanged and R-MSI only adds roots that are not inside an existing root; it never widens or replaces an M1a root.

Burn facts: for an entry of InstallerKind::Burn: bundle_id = the ARP key name (GUID); provider_key = value BundleProviderKey; cache_path = directory of BundleCachePath, accepted only when it is a direct child of the entry's own Package Cache (%ProgramData% for a machine entry, the entry's user's %LOCALAPPDATA% for a per-user entry) named exactly the bundle id (R2a S7). packages = every provider key P whose dependents list bundle_id or provider_key in the machine's records (machine bundle) or the machine's and the entry's own user's records (per-user bundle) (ownership.burn_providers_in, R2a S6); a P named only in the user's records whose product is installed for the machine is left out; product_code = P's key name when it is a GUID, else P's default value (read in the hive of the record) when that is a GUID; cache_dir = LastUsedSource directory when it is a direct child of the entry's own Package Cache named {ProductCode} or {ProductCode}v<version> (R2a S7); other_dependents = the Dependents names minus this bundle's. An MSI child is harvested as MsiFacts only when other_dependents is empty and the product is installed.
Burn roots: the union of R-MSI roots of the harvested MSI children. A child with other dependents contributes nothing (Python Launcher when two Pythons are installed).

System objects (fp.sys): a service, task or firewall rule is recorded when ctx-free ownership holds at harvest time: its ProgramRef is File(f) and f is inside an InstallRoot of the fingerprint (R2a S4: inferred and referenced roots never) or equals one of fp.exes / outside_root_files (ObjectWhy::ProgramInRoot / ProgramIsAppExe), or (services only) its name equals a ServiceInstall row name of the app's own MSI AND its program is inside an InstallRoot (ObjectWhy::MsiServiceRow). The scan side backs OwnedSystemObject only by this record with the same digest, never by a ServiceInstall row name alone (R2a S3). Name similarity is never a reason. Objects blocked by purge_guard::check_object are not recorded.
A multi-action task is recorded only when every Exec action's file is the app's.
Every recorded object stores the identity (C-OBJECT) as read at harvest; the scanner compares digests after the uninstall.

Limits: at most 5,000 components, 20,000 registry rows, 500 system objects per fingerprint; beyond that the list is cut, a warning names the cut, and for components the MSI root rule is not applied at all (a partial component list could hide a foreign client).
No new registry or file walk: everything comes from the two indexes, the app's own tables and the existing refsnap.

packages.title: purge-exec: delete service, with definition backup, probe, completion and undo

model.why: Performs and undoes the deletion of a Windows service.

packages.scope: Implement the six entry points of C-ACT for ExecOp::DeleteService over ServiceBackend, plus the live backend over purge_win::scm and the registry (key tree backup through the existing regbackup module).
rules: validate: read the service. Absent -> Decided(Vanished). Build ServiceIdentity from the registry key (the same fields and source as the scanner), digest must equal the plan's object_fp (else Skipped ChangedSinceScan). check_object with fresh facts must pass (else Skipped GateBlocked{that blocker}). Type driver bits, per-user, delete flag set -> GateBlocked. Dependents (any other service listing it in DependOnService) -> GateBlocked{HasDependents}. State not STOPPED -> GateBlocked{InUse}. Record Stamp::Object and ItemFacts::Object.

prepare: take the regbackup of the whole Services\<name> tree (verified, as any key backup), then query the SCM definition, then re-read the identity; if its digest differs from the validated stamp -> Decided(Skipped ChangedSinceScan) and the backups are left for expiry. Write purge.svcdef/1 with key_backup. Inverse::RecreateService. account_builtin false -> the item was planned Partial; if the plan says Reversibility::Full but account_builtin is false, Decided(Skipped GateBlocked{ReversibilityPartial}).
act: act-time gate of C-ACT (identity digest, check_object, state STOPPED, no dependents - all re-read now), then backend.delete(name). Fault point objdelete.after. Then flush SYSTEM.
complete: Deleted -> Done. Marked (key present with DeleteFlag) -> PendingReboot. Still present without DeleteFlag -> Failed{ObjectApi}.

probe (recovery after a crash between intent and done): service absent -> Done; present with DeleteFlag -> Done(PendingReboot); present, digest equal to the stamp -> NotDone; present, digest different -> Attention.

undo: read_def (verified). If the service exists: with DeleteFlag -> Failed{PendingDelete}; digest equal to the backup's identity and the key tree equal to the key backup -> AlreadyRestored; otherwise Failed{ObjectExists}. If absent: the binary_path's resolved program must be under a root recorded in the journal header, else Failed{ProgramOutsideRoot} (a tampered-with store must not be able to plant a service for an arbitrary binary; the def hash check comes first, this is the second lock). account_builtin false -> Failed{PasswordNeeded} unless the user passed the existing 'allow partial' undo option, in which case the service is created with the account name and no password. Then: create -> fault svcrestore.mid -> apply_config2 (every non-null item) -> apply_security -> restore from key_backup every value and subkey that RESULT.json lists in write_back_needed and that is absent or different (through the existing key-restore code restricted to this one tree) -> flush SYSTEM -> exact-restore check: capture the tree again, compare with key_backup ignoring only RESULT.json scm_owned_values that the spike proved cannot be reproduced; equal -> Restored, else Failed{ValueDiffers} with the first difference named.

A crash at svcrestore.mid leaves a half-configured, never-started service; recovery of an undo re-runs undo: the service then exists and differs -> the module recognises its own partial restore by the journal's undo intent record for this op and continues from apply_config2 instead of failing with ObjectExists. Without that intent record it is ObjectExists.
The restored service is never started. Its Start value is what the backup says.
No path is resolved twice: the name validated is the name acted on; every SCM call opens the service by that name and the digest check uses handles/reads taken after the open of the same step.

packages.title: Scanners COM-CLASS and COM-INTERFACE

model.why: Decides which objects are offered for deletion and which are preselected.

packages.scope: COM-CLASS offers the app's own CLSID, AppID and TypeLib registrations; COM-INTERFACE offers Interface keys that only served the app. Driven by fp.anchors (clsids, appids, typelibs: harvested before the uninstall, including the app's own MSI Class/TypeLib/AppId rows) and by shared-walk hits; there is no walk of CLSID or Interface.
rules: Scanner common rules (S-COMMON, cross_package_notes) apply: reads only through ScanCtx; candidates only through CandidateBuilder and ctx.run sealing; no walker call; a name is never evidence of ownership; when a needed source answers NotCaptured or AccessDenied the scanner emits nothing for that part and adds one scan warning.

Views: every anchor is looked up at HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID\{x}, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\WOW6432Node\CLSID\{x}, HKU\<sid>\Software\Classes\CLSID\{x} and HKU\<sid>\Software\Classes\WOW6432Node\CLSID\{x} for every loaded user; the same four places for Interface; AppID and TypeLib at the places the existing CLASSES_REDIRECTED table says exist per view. Targets are spelled with the real key path, never through HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Classes (a registry link) and never through HKCR.

CLSID key, per view: server = default value of InprocServer32, LocalServer32 or InprocHandler32 resolved with resolve_program rules (LocalServer32 command lines) or as a plain path (InprocServer32). (a) server inside a root or an fp exe, file missing: candidate RegKey/DeleteKey with ComKeyOwnership + DanglingRef -> can be Safe. (b) server inside a root, file present: same candidate without DanglingRef -> Likely. (c) server is a file outside every root that exists: Protected candidate with ReferencedByOtherApp (another product registered the class after us) - listed so the user sees why. (d) server outside every root and missing, or no server subkey: no candidate. (e) InprocServer32 = mscoree.dll with a CodeBase or Assembly value: the server is the CodeBase file path (file:/// form decoded); without CodeBase no candidate. (f) key present in the baseline: no candidate.

A CLSID that any other CLSID names in TreatAs or AutoTreatAs, or that any Interface outside the app names as ProxyStubClsid32 where that Interface is in kb shared IIDs, is Protected (ReferencedByOtherApp / SharedIid).

Is any alias, WOW64 or control-set mapping implemented a second time outside purge-guard?
Ownership index: where does 'could not read' turn into 'owns nothing'? Stale clients, permanent components, per-user contexts, truncated tables, a user-writable cache.

resolve_program: get an interpreter, a host, an ambiguous unquoted path or a relative path accepted as the app's program.
Path-keyed stores: bare names, UNC, prefix siblings, ROT13 edge cases, MuiCache resource names.

decisions: D1 No new action kind for MSI-registration cleanup or COM registrations. They are DeleteKey/DeleteValue on registry targets behind narrow guard exemptions. Reason: the M2 registry executor already has backup, gate, durability and exact restore for keys and values; a second path would need all of it again. Alternative rejected: MsiZap-style typed op.

D2 Typed objects use the existing convention (Service | Task | FirewallRule target, Action::DeleteKey) and map to three new ExecOps. Reason: plan hash, order stages and policy scope already know this pair. Alternative rejected: new Action variants (changes purge.planhash/0).

D3 Object identity is one digest defined in purge-model and carried in the plan as object_fp, outside the plan hash. The executor refuses a typed item without it. Reason: binds the act to what the scanner saw, the M2 rule for files and keys. Alternative rejected: re-deriving ownership in the executor (second copy of scanner logic).

D4 Services and firewall rules are read from the registry through RegistrySource; tasks through one new SystemSource method. Reason: fixtures and rig snaps already capture the registry, so scanners are testable offline; Task Scheduler has no documented registry form. Alternative rejected: SCM and firewall COM enumeration in the source layer.

D5 MSI component clients and key paths come from Installer\UserData\<sid>\Components in the registry, all users and contexts, one bounded read. Reason: no per-component API calls, works offline, gives the 'more than one client' rule for free. Alternative rejected: MsiEnumClientsExW per component (plan 5.5).

D6 The 'more than one MSI client' rule: any client other than the target product blocks, including stale clients of products no longer installed and the permanent marker. Reason: a stale client cannot be told from a product installed for another user profile that is not loaded. Alternative rejected: discounting clients that are not in the inventory.

D7 File ownership by key paths and directories, not by Directory/File tables. Reason: no Formatted or directory resolution of other products' packages, which is where wrong answers come from. Cost stated in plan_corrections.
D8 MSI rows that cannot be resolved exactly are dropped and counted; an unreadable package is a soft block (MsiPackageUnreadable), never 'owns nothing'.

D9 MSI install folder from component key paths: at least two key-path files (or one plus corroboration), lowest common ancestor, no foreign component in the folder, never a system folder. Reason: fixes the 7-Zip MSI case without trusting names. Alternative rejected: Directory table TARGETDIR resolution.

D10 A system object is Safe only when it was recorded at harvest with the same digest, its program was the app's, and the program file is gone now. Otherwise at most Likely. Reason: a service whose binary still exists may still be in use by leftover files the user keeps.
D11 Nothing is stopped. A running service or task is skipped as InUse (M2 decision kept until the UI can ask for consent in M3).
D12 Drivers, per-user services, svchost-hosted services with a DLL under the Windows folder, tasks under \Microsoft\Windows, AppX-bound and resource-named firewall rules are never offered.

D13 Services with dependents are blocked even when the dependent is the app's own. Reason: deleting in dependency order across items needs plan-level ordering that M1b does not have. Second run removes the rest.
D14 Firewall delete only by InstanceID over WMI; identity and exact-restore check from the registry string. No registry write, no netsh, no PowerShell, no delete by name.
D15 Undo of a typed object refuses to create anything whose program lies outside the roots recorded in the journal header. Reason: a tampered store must not be usable to plant a service or task.

D16 The one reference walk is computed once in the pipeline and shared through ScanCtx.ext; the ownership index likewise. Scanners have per-scanner key-open budgets checked in unit tests, and xtask forbids walker calls in scanners.
D17 The MSI table cache on disk is used only from an admin-only-writable directory; otherwise the cache is in memory for the run.
D18 Path-keyed stores: a value is the app's only by a full path in its name. All such stores are value containers in the guard.
D19 Tracing keys and WER reports are at most Likely in M1b (name or content evidence without Tier A scope). EventLog sources are Safe only when the app's own MSI declares them.
D20 Policy version m1b.1. The only band changes for M1a apps come from added MSI blockers and the new scanners; proven by replay (K16).
D21 Fingerprint, plan and journal schemas keep their ids; all additions are optional fields or new enum variants.
D22 crates_files in this document are repository-relative (M2_DESIGN used absolute paths of the main checkout). Reason: implementation agents work in their own worktrees.
risks_and_questions: Q1 (user) May services, tasks and firewall rules be preselected at all? Default: yes, under D10 only (recorded at harvest, program gone, full undo). The stricter choice is 'never preselected in M1b': one line in purge-policy, no other change.

Q2 (user) If the spike shows a firewall rule cannot be re-created with its old id: accept restore under a new id as Partial (never preselected), or leave firewall rules report-only? Default: Partial with new id.
Q3 (user) Services running under a user account (stored password): offer as Partial (not preselected, undo needs the password re-entered by hand), or never offer? Default: offer as Partial.
Q4 (user) Which Temurin and PowerShell versions does the rig pin? Default: Temurin 21 LTS JDK x64 MSI and the current PowerShell 7 LTS x64 MSI at the time M1B-RIG-GUEST runs.

Q5 (user) Is +2.5 s warm on scan and on harvest acceptable on the 591-program host (9 s and 11 s today)? Default: yes for M1b; the cut, if wanted, is a cache of the component read keyed by the Components key times, which needs its own review.

Risk: the spike may show that SCM re-creation does not reproduce the Services key byte for byte (value types, Security blob). Mitigation in the design: write-back of backed-up values through the registry restore code, and an explicit list of values that cannot be reproduced; if that list is not empty the gate criterion K11 must name them.
Risk: MSI uninstallers of the six real apps leave little; most new scanners are proven only by traps. The trap list is therefore reviewed (R4) as carefully as code.
Risk: M1B-FRAMEWORK and M1B-MODEL touch files many others read. Both make compile-only fallout edits elsewhere; merge them first in their waves.
Risk: the Components subtree can be large on machines with Visual Studio or Office (hundreds of thousands of components). The memory cap marks the rest unreadable, which only adds soft blocks.
Risk: Task Scheduler COM from an unelevated scan lists only tasks the user can read. Unreadable tasks are never attributed; elevated scans see more. The gate runs elevated.
cut_or_move: Firewall AppIso (package-bound) rules: cut. Windows owns them and removes them with the package; offering them risks other packages' rules.
SYS-APPX all-users removal and deprovisioning: move to M3/M4. It needs a target scope in the plan and consent in the UI; M1b only closes guards (M1B-S-APPX).
MSI Directory/File table file ownership: move to M4 if the gate shows a gap. Key paths plus directory components cover the cases the rig has.
Cached .msi/.msp under the Windows Installer folder for gone products: move to M4. Windows-managed directory, needs its own trap set.
VS Code user-beside-system (shared VSCode.<ext> ProgIDs attributed through the installer log): keep deferred to M4. It is an Inno case and unrelated to MSI, COM or system objects.
FS-WER and Tracing as preselected items: not in M1b (Likely only). Revisit with the M4 privacy scanners.
Removing a service together with its dependents in one run: move to M3, with the stop-with-consent flow.
PowerShell and Temurin on Purge-CleanPro: not in the gate (G8 runs 7zip, python, vcredist there). Add if a second-OS difference shows up.
cross_package_notes: S-COMMON (every scanner package): a scanner reads only through ScanCtx (reg, fs, sys, fp, ext); it never opens the registry or the disk by itself, never calls walker or refscan, never spawns a process. It builds candidates only through CandidateBuilder and returns them through ctx.run, which seals them. A name (service, task, rule, product, key, file stem) is never evidence of ownership; ownership comes from a program path inside a root or exe set, an installer record, or a harvest record. A value is offered whole only when all its content is the app's. Missing data means no candidate, never a guess.

File ownership: within a wave no two packages own the same file. Integration packages (the only ones that edit shared hot files) are M1B-MODEL (wave 1, compile-only fallout), M1B-FRAMEWORK (wave 3: framework.rs, ScanCtx sites, pipeline.rs), M1B-X-INTEG (wave 4: executor routing), M1B-SCAN-INTEG (wave 5: catalog.rs, pipeline.rs, xtask). No other package edits a Cargo.toml, a lib.rs module list, catalog.rs, pipeline.rs, framework.rs, execute.rs, undo.rs or recover.rs.
Merge order inside a wave: integration and model packages first, then the rest in any order. Each package rebases on the merged wave before its final test run.

Model routing: critical -> Fable, medium effort; high -> Opus, high effort; medium -> Opus, medium effort; trivial -> Sonnet; VM campaign babysitting -> Haiku. Every critical package gets a Fable review (review_points), whatever it costs in tokens.

Paths in crates_files are relative to the repository root. Contracts named C-... are in the top-level contracts object; a package implements or consumes them exactly as written. A package that finds a contract impossible stops and reports; it does not change the contract on its own.

Canonical forms: every path and key comparison uses purge-guard canonicalisation and fold. No package writes its own WOW64, HKCR, <sid>_Classes or ControlSet mapping. Targets under 32-bit Classes are spelled HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\WOW6432Node\..., never through HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Classes.
Errors from sources: NotCaptured and AccessDenied mean 'unknown'. Unknown never removes a blocker, never opens an exemption and never makes a candidate.

Executor rules carried over from M2 without change: release build has no executor path (feature rig-exec); --confirm = SHA-256(plan_hash || selection_hash); nothing is stopped, closed or restarted; backups are verified before intent; hives are flushed before done, group_end, commit and undo_done; exit code 12 precedence.

VM rig rules: tests run only on the rig VMs and need no approval; official downloads only; never touch the clone; restore snapshots after each mode. No VM step runs on the host. G7 is the only host measurement and is read-only (harvest and scan, no execute).

Test names in a package entry are required tests. A test must assert what its name says; reviewers check this. Tests marked hostile model an attacker or a broken third-party installer and must fail before the fix they guard is written.

Limits known at design time, to be listed in docs/M1B_GATE.md if still true: patches and transforms that add MSI rows are not read; non-key-path files are protected by directory, not by file; a service with dependents needs two runs; tasks unreadable to the scanning user are never attributed; cached installer files are not offered.
